questions.q: The graph of pressure P and volume V of $1$ mole of an ideal gas at constant temperature is
questions.solution:
According to the ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$.

For $1$ mole of an ideal gas at constant temperature, $n$ and $T$ are constant. Therefore, $PV = \text{constant}$.

This implies that pressure $P$ is inversely proportional to volume $V$, which can be written as $P \propto \dfrac{1}{V}$.

The mathematical relationship $PV = \text{constant}$ represents a rectangular hyperbola.

Among the given graphs, Graph-IV correctly depicts a rectangular hyperbola, which is the characteristic $P-V$ curve for an isothermal process.

For oxygen molecules; $\frac{v_0}{v_{\text {rms }}}=\frac{\sqrt{\frac{r_0 R T}{M}}}{\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M}}}=\sqrt{\frac{r_0}{3}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Pressure of ideal gas at constant volume is proportional to
options: average potential energy of the molecules
average kinetic energy of the molecules
questions.solution:
Gay Lussac's law states that the pressure of a
fixed mass of a gas at constant volume is directly proportional to the temperature.
i.e. $p \propto T$
or
$p \propto \frac{1}{2} K_B T$
Since kinetic energy of the molecules is directly proportional to the temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
One mole of \( 4 \) gas is heated at constant pressure starting at \( 27{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C} . \) How much energy must be
added to the gas as heat to double its volume?
questions.solution:
(C)
At constant pressure it volume is doubled, temperate gets doubled,
\( T_{1}=300 \mathrm{k}, T_{2}=600 \mathrm{k} \)
hence \( \Delta T=600-300=300 \mathrm{k} \)
\( Q=n c_{p} \Delta T=1 \times \frac{7}{2} R \times 300=1050 R \)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Pressure of an ideal gas is increased by keeping temperature constant. The kinetic energy of
molecules
options: Increses or decreases depending on the nature of gas
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy of molecules depends only on the temperature, that is,
\( \mathrm{K} \propto \mathrm{T} \)
Therefore, if the pressure of an ideal gas is increased by keeping temperature constant, then kinetic energy of molecules
remains same.
